previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and a history of antiphospholipid syndrome presented with atypical chest pain radiating from her back to her chest, accompanied by shortness of breath and dizziness. The pain did not respond to nitroglycerin and was initially concerning for cardiac ischemia, but EKG and serial troponins were stable and consistent with her baseline due to chronic kidney disease. A CT pulmonary angiogram ruled out pulmonary embolism. The chest pain resolved during the admission and was attributed to esophageal spasm. Due to recent IV contrast administration, she was monitored for possible dialysis, but the renal team confirmed it was not needed. She remained stable, continued her home medications, and was discharged home the following morning with plans to resume outpatient dialysis and follow up with her gastroenterologist and rheumatologist regarding esophageal spasms and hand tenderness possibly due to gout.
